ns1:item.ns1:title: Accounting for vertical variations in urban heat and air pollution exposure
ns1:item.content:encoded:
Nature Reviews Earth & Environment, Published online: 22 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s43017-026-00835-6

Urban heat and air pollution exposure are commonly assessed at ground level; however, their intensity can vary with height. Thus, in fast-growing dense high-rise cities, vertically resolved air quality, heat, and epidemiological evidence is needed to support floor-based health risk assessments.
ns1:item.dc:title: Accounting for vertical variations in urban heat and air pollution exposure

Jos Lelieveld
